subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own this experimental, provenance-aware Claw removal lifecycle—including package cleanup selection and session/workspace deletion—or should the scope be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The patch is not merely a mechanical CLI addition: it defines the ownership and recovery policy for deleting agent-associated state and packages, which cannot be safely settled from tests alone.

options.title: Sponsor the full experimental lifecycle
options.body: Confirm that core should own the plan-bound status/remove contract after final-head proof demonstrates retention, selected cleanup, and forced-conflict behavior.

options.title: Narrow the first landing
options.body: Keep status and conservative release-only removal, while deferring referenced-resource uninstall and broader cleanup policy to a follow-up after the RFC direction is settled.

options.title: Pause the stacked lifecycle series
options.body: Defer this slice until the RFC establishes the intended long-term ownership, recovery, and deletion-history policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the full experimental lifecycle
recommendation.body: Confirm that core should own the plan-bound status/remove contract after final-head proof demonstrates retention, selected cleanup, and forced-conflict behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing contact for the coherent stacked Claws feature series and its implementation contract.
